reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Tell us, our master, and instruct us about these three vessels that [were swept out] and were discharged from above, and how they were discharged and separated from all the rulers who are arranged in the heavens. For it is a necessity for us to know the manner in which the three vessels have been discharged, while the rulers were flourishing in their body.
when these vessels were discharged, they were discharged in [great] slaughter, but those [who separated] these vessels from them.

They are like the form of a man who has fallen into a purulent sickness. Other wounds and diseases are in his body, and even bile and other poisons are in his inner limbs. He achieves good health by a wise doctor, who gives him one remedy to drink that causes his purulent sickness to break out above, and gives him another medicine to drink that causes his sickness to discharge below, and he gives him yet another medicine to drink that cures his wounds for him [ ... ] calmly and silently.

Through the skill of a wise doctor, with his effective medicines to consume that take away all sicknesses in this manner and dissolve all magic, the doctors shall [ ... ] they work cures through the aroma of the medicine, other wounds [that are in] what is hidden, they at last tear them out from [the body, and they are] manifested above and below [and they are healed through] the aroma of edible medicines that were placed upon them.

This is also what these vessels of water, of darkness and of fire are like, which are hidden in the body of all the rulers above; while the Living Spirit is like the wise doctor. These three healing drugs are the three garments that the Living Spirit assumes upon his body: of wind, of water, and of fire. Through them he has set in order the things below. For by those three garments he has been displayed to the rulers who are above, with hard-heartedness, with shaking and fear, with derangement; from them he discharged the three vessels, those of water, of darkness and of fire.

The case of these vessels is just like a child who is in his mother's womb and is swathed by seven garments. The first is the marrow, the second is the bones, the third is the tendons, the fourth is the flesh, the fifth the veins, the sixth the blood, the seventh the skin of the body that covers him. The other garment also [ ... / ... in the womb of his mother. His mother also is just like] this child. The marrow and the bones, the sinews and flesh, the veins and blood and skin, together with the garment that she wears and the linen that swathes her, total nine. Together with the nine of the child, these and the others, they shall complete and make eighteen garments. Now, you shall find the soul of this child is entwined within all these.

And look see: When the smell of the action of the demon, which brings about the stench of birth, will reveal the child; immediately [he] shall [open] all [these things] and it emerges from a crack that has become visible, while no tear nor wound occurs in the body of the child. In the same way as this child opens up the womb of his mother, so is it also with these vessels of water, of darkness and of fire. fills.explanation: The text consistently pairs "swept out" with "discharged" throughout the chapter (¶9, ¶10, ¶13, ¶17, ¶18, ¶33), and the spiritual reading confirms the vessels "were cast down" as a parallel action to discharge.
The spiritual reading says "violent upheaval," and "great slaughter" is the natural-plane intensifier modifying the noun "slaughter" in the Kephalaia's register of cosmic conflict.
The agents (the Living Spirit and divine forces) separated the three vessels from the rulers; the spiritual reading confirms the action of removing the containing forms from the dominant persuasions.

The spiritual reading indicates "other wounds within what is hidden"; the wounds exist inside the hidden interior, and "that are in" connects "other wounds" to "what is hidden" as their concealed location.

The doctors tear hidden wounds out from the body, and then those wounds become visible; the spiritual reading confirms manifestation in the higher and lower faculties, corresponding to "above and below" in the natural register.

After the hidden wounds are manifested above and below, they are healed through the aroma of medicines; the spiritual reading confirms healing through the perception of nourishing truths applied upon them.

fills.original: ... / ... in the womb of his mother. His mother also is just like

fills.explanation: The child is the subject who acts to open the womb; the later text confirms "this child opens up the womb of his mother," making "he" the grammatical subject of "shall open."
The birth metaphor requires the child to open the layers of covering; the later text explicitly says "this child opens up the womb of his mother," confirming "open" as the verb.
The editor's "these things" correctly refers to the eighteen garments/coverings just enumerated; the child opens all these layers to emerge, and the spiritual reading confirms this reference.
The Living Spirit moved the waters from the rulers, and the following clause explains what these waters are; "for" introduces the explanatory clause "they are the poison and death."
The Living Spirit was revealed to the rulers through the garment of wind; "to them" supplies the dative object required by "was revealed," paralleling the structure of ¶8 and ¶10.

The Living Spirit stripped off the garments one by one and cast the vessels down; "cast them down to the earth" follows the chapter's consistent vocabulary for the descent of vessels (cf. ¶10, ¶17, ¶18).

fills.fill: nor in all flesh, for it has set i
fills.explanation: The pattern "trees, fruits, and all flesh" recurs throughout ¶16–19; "for" introduces the transition to the three sub-categories, and "it has set i" is the surviving readable portion completing "itself."

The editor's choice matches perfectly: "the vessel of water" is the chapter's consistent term for the containing form of falsified truth, and the conditional parallels ¶17 (vessel of darkness) and ¶18 (fire).
The parallel in ¶17 says "the torrents that will continue to flow down from above to the earth," establishing the direction of flow for the conditional in ¶16.

The exact parallel in ¶17 reads "the drops of darkness, which will drip down from it"; "drip" is the verb consistently paired with "droplets/drops" throughout the chapter's three parallel conditional passages.

The parallel in ¶17 says "would have multiplied" and ¶19 says "would have multiplied in the tree and in fruit"; "sprouted and multiplied" is the natural doublet describing the increase of disordered desire.
The parallel conditional in ¶17 uses "again" to introduce the consequence clause ("again the drops of darkness..."), establishing the pattern for the fire conditional in ¶18.
The parallel structure in ¶16–17 describes torrents flowing and drops dripping down from above; the conditional construction requires "would have dripped down from above through the torrent."
The editor's "The third" correctly continues the enumeration of twelve deeds (first in ¶14, second in ¶21, fourth in ¶23), following the chapter's consistent numbering pattern.
The third deed describes the heavens' burden being relieved; "was" supplies the passive verb linking "burden" to "relieved from the weight-carriers."

The weight-carriers are defined by their function of bearing the heavens and firmaments; "that bear them" specifies this function and provides the natural referent for "them" (the heavens and firmaments named at the start of the sentence).
The consistent pattern of the twelve deeds uses "That" to introduce purpose clauses (cf. "The eighth: That great enclosures..."), and "the" is required before "nature."
The tenth deed describes the vessels as agents of purification at the end of the universe; the fire "burns all things" completes the eschatological image of final consuming purification.
Following the consistent pattern of the twelve deeds using "That" + subject to introduce purpose clauses, and "they" refers to the vessels or divine agents making the crossing.

The eleventh deed describes a crossing; "the entire ruling-power will pass over to the outer land" completes the eschatological passage, echoing "make a crossing" and the spiritual reading's reference to passage of the governing authority.
The simile compares the aeons of light to a rich man who has no cause for envy; "like" introduces this comparison in the Kephalaia's typical manner of teaching through similitude.
The aeons of light are outside the inner worlds (them), dwelling in the place of peace; "them" refers to the inner regions just described, and "in" introduces the location of the aeons.

The phrase "the place of rest and of peace" creates a doublet parallel to "the place of honour and grace" that follows, and "rest" paired with "peace" is a standard formula in Manichaean descriptions of the realm of light.

The unclean things are hidden from the aeons of light by the wall of fire and displayed only within its interior space; "midst" denotes the enclosed region inside the wall of fire where impurity is confined.

The doublet "power and authority" is a standard Kephalaia pairing for divine governance; the three words of life are set over the vessels in great power and authority to watch over them at the last time.
